userFeedback: None of these five makes the user linger. Only the original account's two pinned images do.
currentRole: Research examples only, not user-endorsed aesthetic targets. Do not treat awards, technical quality, or assistant preference as evidence of the user's positive response.
purpose: External reference research after repeated generated images were judged too flat.
userPriorities: rich detail and HDR-like tonal depth
scope: Publicly available photographer and competition source pages. All five images visually inspected in the in-app browser; metadata verified through primary sources. No original media files downloaded.
referenceBoundary: Use only techniques, optical effects, light hierarchy and general artistic principles; do not reproduce these subject combinations, framing or arrangements in later original images.
technicalUncertainty: A photographic appearance or rich tonal range is not evidence of HDR merging. Specific editing or compositing workflows are not claimed where the source does not disclose them.

references.title: Aureus
references.creator: Ray Collins
references.observed: Close view of a curled wave, pale-gold light across long tactile ridges, deep near-black upper shadows and a small opening at the left.
techniqueReferences: warm light used to sculpt volume
a large coherent curve with smaller surface details
close framing that makes water the primary form

references.title: Golden Arch
references.creator: Ray Collins
references.observed: A hollow breaking wave occupies most of the frame; light penetrates the thin crest and suspended spray, with a dark wave base and blue background.
techniqueReferences: hollow volume and looming foreground mass
references.note: Selected for form and spatial force rather than as a warm-palette example.

references.title: Ignis
references.creator: Rachael Talibart
references.observed: Elongated orange-gold reflection strokes run through deep dark water; selective softness and unequal spacing make the surface resemble moving flame.
techniqueReferences: abstract form emerging from water motion
uneven density of light against dark negative space

references.title: The World is Going Upside Down
references.creator: Thomas Vijayan
references.award: Nature TTL Photographer of the Year 2021 overall winner
references.observed: An orangutan and converging tree trunks occupy the center of an apparently skyward view; reflected sky and forest in water create a second spatial reading.
techniqueReferences: strong converging lines with a readable living focal point
references.note: Selected for a compelling reflection relationship, not a uniformly warm palette.

references.title: The Embrace
references.creator: Sergey Gorshkov
references.award: Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2020 Adult Grand Title Winner
references.observed: An Amur tiger stands against and grips a large trunk, face turned into the bark; its warm body is set within a dark forest.
techniqueReferences: emotion readable through an observed physical gesture
warm subject against a quieter dark environment
tactile fur and bark supporting the relationship
references.behaviorContext: Official description explains scent-marking; an embrace is a visual reading rather than a claim about the animal's emotion.
